title: Microsoft Purview Insider Risk Management: Policy Recommendation panel
summary: Hold: Microsoft documents PowerShell for managing role group membership, so that automation control must not be reported as undocumented. The membership path also stops before the documented editing controls. The rollout dates and enabled-by-default description match Microsoft's notice and roadmap.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The panel processes existing policy configurations and organisational signals within IRM, introducing additional processing of customer data signals.
claims.quote: The feature analyzes existing policy configurations and organizational signals within Insider Risk Management to generate recommendations, which introduces additional processing of customer data signals.

claims.claim: The panel uses analytics-driven intelligence and correlated signals to generate recommendations.
claims.quote: The policy recommendation panel uses analytics-driven intelligence to identify gaps in policy coverage and generate recommendations based on correlated signals.

claims.claim: The announced change is a recommendation view over existing policies rather than a new detection policy.
claims.quote: The panel will analyze existing policies and identify potential gaps in coverage. Administrators will receive recommendations to create policies

claims.claim: Neither the notice nor the roadmap says the panel creates or edits policies without an administrator.
claims.quote: Administrators will receive recommendations to create policies addressing risks such as data leakage, data theft, and risky AI usage. Existing policies and configurations remain unchanged.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not yet describe this specific Policy Recommendation panel.
claims.quote: Searched: '"policy recommendation panel" "Insider"'. Opened IRM policies, analytics settings, permissions, plan and configure pages; results describe existing analytics recommendations, not this panel.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; controls[0].api; Risk assessment; Governance controls
claims.claim: No UI setting or automation operation is documented to hide, disable or limit the new panel.
claims.quote: Searched: '"policy recommendation panel" disable roles signals analytics administrative units'; 'purview insider risk management policy recommendation panel settings disable licensing analytics API Add-RoleGroupMember'. Opened IRM policies and analytics settings; no panel switch or API found.

claims.claim: The analytics setting is reached in Microsoft Purview portal through Settings > Insider Risk Management > Insider risk settings > Analytics.
claims.quote: Select Settings in the upper-right corner of the page. Select Insider Risk Management to go to the Insider Risk Management settings. Under Insider risk settings, select Analytics, and then turn off the setting.

claims.claim: No API or PowerShell operation is documented for changing the insider risk analytics scanning setting.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Insider Risk" "analytics" "PowerShell" settings API'; '"Insider Risk Management" "analytics" "Graph" settings API disable'; '"Insider Risk Management" "analytics" "Set-" "PowerShell"'. Read analytics settings and configure pages; only portal operations found.

claims.claim: Enabling or disabling analytics requires membership in Insider Risk Management, Insider Risk Management Admins or Microsoft 365 Global admin.
claims.quote: To turn off insider risk analytics, you must be a member of the Insider Risk Management, Insider Risk Management Admins, or Microsoft 365 Global admin role group.

claims.claim: The analytics scanning setting has tenant-wide scope.
claims.quote: Selecting Run scan turns on analytics scanning for your organization

claims.claim: Existing insider risk analytics scans Microsoft 365 audit logs and other sources.
claims.quote: Analytics scans several sources for risk management activity to help you identify insights into potential areas of risk. Microsoft 365 audit logs: Included in all scans

claims.where: controls[1].governs; What's changing; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Existing analytics results provide policy recommendations.
claims.quote: Policy recommendations from analytics ... If you decide to act on analytics scan results for data leaks or data theft by departing users policies, you can even configure a quick policy based on these results.

claims.claim: Whether the new panel depends on the existing analytics setting or uses its scan is not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: '"policy recommendation panel" disable roles signals analytics administrative units'; '"Insider Risk Management" "analytics" "Graph" settings API disable'. Read policies and analytics settings and supplied notice; none links this panel to the analytics toggle or scan.

claims.claim: Settings > Roles and groups > Roles groups > Insider Risk Management is the complete path to the membership control.
claims.quote: Select the Insider Risk Management role group, then select Edit. Select Choose users, then select the checkboxes for all the users you want to add to the role group.
claims.fix: Extend controls[2].ui.path and the rendered table path to 'Settings > Roles and groups > Roles groups > Insider Risk Management > Edit > Choose users', as documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/insider-risk-management-permissions. The current path stops before membership can be changed.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented automation for managing Insider Risk Management role group membership.
claims.quote: Use the Add-RoleGroupMember cmdlet to add members to a management role group. ... The Identity parameter specifies the role group to add a member to. ... The Member parameter specifies who you want to add to the role group.
claims.fix: Replace controls[2].api null with kind 'powershell', call 'Add-RoleGroupMember -Identity "Insider Risk Management" -Member <user-UPN>', and docs 'https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/exchangepowershell/add-rolegroupmember?view=exchange-ps'. Name Security & Compliance PowerShell in the note; the reference lists Security & Compliance applicability for Identity and Member. Update the rendered automation cell and cite the reference.

claims.claim: The Insider Risk Management and Insider Risk Management Admins role groups can configure policies and settings.
claims.quote: | Actions | Insider Risk Management | Insider Risk Management Admins | ... | Configure policies and settings | Yes | Yes | No | No | No | No |

claims.quote: After you assign admin units to members of role groups, those members become restricted administrators and have limited access to Insider Risk Management settings, policies, and user data in the organization.

claims.claim: Accessing existing analytics insights requires being an unrestricted administrator.
claims.quote: You must be an unrestricted administrator to access analytics insights.
